title: Recheck eager improvements under production graph execution
applies_when: A change saves Python dispatch or launch overhead, uses a runtime override, or routes on tensor shape while production uses compilation or CUDA graph replay.
lesson: Compare baseline and candidate in the same production execution mode and verify the changed path executes there. Graph replay can remove Python allocation/dispatch, but device fills initializing constants inside capture can still replay. Distinguish host work from captured CUDA work using an actual trace; fewer kernels need not improve latency. Report startup and capture separately from steady-state latency. When dispatch needs the logical phase or valid row count, verify it still receives that information under padded or compiled execution.
avoid_when: An eager diagnostic cannot establish the sign of a graph-mode improvement. Fewer captured kernels are not automatically material whole-workload gains. A tiny Torch constant probe does not qualify an attention backend, mutation/stream lifetime, supported hardware or model correctness. Do not add graph-specific machinery to an eager-only workload.

evidence.note: PyTorch documents fixed replay arguments, reduced CPU overhead and omitted CPU work during replay. Production routing and performance conclusions remain candidate-specific hypotheses.

Sanitized native Torch 2.11 CUDA graph experiment: unchanged Python counters, exact scalar outputs, three retained fill kernels absent after precreation. Twelve order-balanced micro pairs show no stable latency gain; not SGLang/native-attention or E2E qualification. Mutable example branch, not an immutable upstream benchmark.
